title: Settings
subtitle: Clinic-wide configuration. Changes apply to every dentist in the clinic.

chart.readOnly: The chart settings are managed by the clinic owner. You can view them here.

detail.title: Dental / tooth chart
detail.intro: Choose how much detail the chart records. This affects the chart everywhere in the application — the visit workspace, the patient profile and every tooth panel. Existing records are never altered; surface detail already captured is simply not displayed while simple view is on.

simple.label: Simple tooth view
simple.body: The tooth is charted as a whole. Fewer targets, faster charting, and a calmer chart — right for clinics that do not record surface detail.

surface.label: Surface view
surface.body: Each tooth exposes its five surfaces ({{m}}, {{d}}, {{b}}, {{l}} and {{o}} or {{i}}). Services can be scoped to the exact surfaces treated.

toast.simple: Simple tooth view enabled. The chart now works at whole-tooth level everywhere.
toast.surface: Surface view enabled. Teeth can now be charted by individual surface.

notation.title: Tooth notation
notation.intro: Which numbering the chart, tooth picker and tooth history show. The stored record never changes: every tooth is always saved by its FDI code, so switching just relabels the chart, with nothing to migrate.

fdi.label: FDI notation
fdi.body: Two-digit codes by quadrant — #11 to #48 for permanent teeth, #51 to #85 for primary. The system most dental software uses.

universal.label: Universal notation
universal.body: Permanent teeth numbered 1–32, primary teeth lettered A–T.

toast.fdi: FDI notation enabled. Tooth numbers switch to FDI two-digit codes everywhere.
toast.universal: Universal notation enabled. Tooth numbers switch to Universal notation (1–32, A–T) everywhere.

orientation.title: Chart orientation
orientation.intro: Which side of the screen the patient's right-hand quadrants sit on. This flips the numbering direction, the R/L side markers and the left/right arrow-key order together, so the chart always stays internally consistent.

patient_right_on_right.label: Patient's right on the right
patient_right_on_right.body: Numbering runs right to left across the screen, so tooth #1 and the upper right quadrant sit on the right. Matches how many clinicians read a chart while seated at the chair.

patient_right_on_left.label: Patient's right on the left
patient_right_on_left.body: The textbook patient-facing convention: you view the arch as if facing the patient, so their right side falls on your left and numbering runs left to right.

toast.patient_right_on_right: Patient's right now on the right. The chart, its side markers and keyboard order all follow this setting.
toast.patient_right_on_left: Patient's right now on the left. The chart, its side markers and keyboard order all follow this setting.

dentition.title: Dentition
dentition.intro: Not a setting — the chart follows each patient's age automatically, so no one has to remember to switch modes before examining a child. One chart serves all three stages: every column is an anatomical position holding whichever tooth is actually present.

primary.body: Twenty primary teeth, lettered A–T. Permanent molar positions show as not yet erupted.

mixed.body: Permanent incisors and first molars alongside primary canines and molars, in one chart. Each position shows the tooth actually present.
